key_insight: The paper shows that quantum selected configuration interaction can be made more practical by swapping in a lower-cost LCNot-UCCSD initialization and adding an RBM-based generative recovery step.
engineering_relevance: This reduces classical preprocessing overhead and strengthens hybrid quantum-classical workflows for molecular simulation, including DMET-based drug discovery targets.
method: LCNot-UCCSD replaces LUCJ-style CCSD initialization with MP2-amplitude seeding for lower scaling.
QSCI-RBM uses a Restricted Boltzmann Machine to recover configurations as a compact generative subspace model.
The workflow is tested in simulator-based molecular simulations and embedded in DMET for larger chemically relevant systems.
evidence_signal: The methods were evaluated on eight STO-3G molecules across 14 artificial error levels with 100 runs each, plus N2 potential-energy scans in cc-pVDZ and DMET cases for Amantadine and the SARS-CoV-2 main protease/Carmofur complex.
watch_item: Results are from an ideal state-vector simulator and controlled artificial errors, so hardware noise and scaling on real devices remain open implementation risks.
paper_title: Bridging the NISQ and Fault-Tolerant Regimes: Generative-ML-Assisted Quantum Selected CI for Molecular Simulations
